decks.name: LeetCode #226 - Invert Binary Tree
decks.description: Invert a binary tree by swapping left and right children at every node

cards.question: Invert Binary Tree: Given the root of a binary tree, invert the tree, and return its root. Inverting a binary tree means swapping the left and right children of all nodes in the tree.

solutions.name: Breadth First Search
solutions.explanation: Use BFS with queue to traverse tree level by level. For each node, swap its left and right children, then add children to queue for processing. Process all nodes until queue is empty. Returns inverted tree. Iterative approach with O(n) space for queue in worst case of complete tree.

solutions.spaceDescription: Queue stores nodes at current level, worst case O(n) for complete binary tree with n/2 nodes at last level
solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given tree [4,2,7,1,3,6,9]: Queue starts with [4]. Process 4: swap children, queue=[2,7]. Process 2: swap children, queue=[7,1,3]. Process 7: swap children, queue=[1,3,6,9]. Continue until queue empty. Result: [4,7,2,9,6,3,1].

solutions.name: Depth First Search
solutions.explanation: Use recursive DFS to traverse tree. Base case returns None for null nodes. For each node, swap left and right children, then recursively invert left and right subtrees. Clean recursive solution that processes tree top-down. Uses O(n) space for recursion stack in worst case of skewed tree.

solutions.name: Iterative DFS
solutions.explanation: Use iterative DFS with stack to avoid recursion. Push root to stack, then repeatedly pop node, swap its children, and push children to stack. Similar to BFS but uses stack (LIFO) instead of queue (FIFO), resulting in depth-first processing. Same O(n) time and space as other approaches but iterative.
